message.content:
Review: The design is mostly clear and logically tied to the stated research question. It distinguishes the primary randomized coupling comparison from the drive-only control and optional disorder condition, explains the synchronized measurements and onset analysis, and correctly treats runs rather than time samples as independent units. The rationale also separates the published claim and aggregate observations from what the proposed study can establish.

Feedback: A few details remain open to interpretation. Specify the coupling settings and how the pilot will establish that they produce distinct coarsening rates without compromising stable operation. Give the planned observation duration and the numerical or otherwise operational definitions for the spectral background, detection threshold, qualifying windows, and persistence. Clarify whether drive-only and disorder conditions are separate follow-up comparisons or part of a factorial design, and how their results will be analyzed. Finally, name the planned model family or estimands for onset time, persistence, and repeated measurements; “accounting for” these features does not fully specify the analysis. These can be preregistered after pilot calibration, but stating that explicitly would make the procedure easier to reproduce.

Rating (1-5): 4
